narratives.Description: design(scm): trust provisioned GitHub credentials and enforce explicit worker assignments
narratives.Overview:
- **R0 — Trust provisioning; do not authorize by runtime.** Unassigned processes use gh's effective credentials for the target host. Local, CI, cloud, ambiguous runtime, socket presence/absence, and probe failure have identical authentication policy. Remove DEFT_GITHUB_AUTH_MODE, hasExplicitHostGhSelection, EXPLICIT_SELECTION_REMEDIATION, and runtime/socket decisions from auth admission. Retain runtime diagnostics and unrelated runtime consumers. Do not add a replacement trust flag, socket exception, or platform allowlist.

- **R1 — Resolve the actual target and source.** Resolve the command's GitHub host and owner/repository with explicit target precedence over inferred context, consistently honoring gh's GH_REPO/GH_HOST and repository context. Probes and operations use the same resolved target and environment. For github.com and ghe.com subdomains, nonempty GH_TOKEN then GITHUB_TOKEN override the host's store; for GitHub Enterprise Server, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN then GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN do so. A token for another host family is neither this operation's injected source nor its source conflict. An applicable invalid token fails without fallback to stored credentials. Report the effective source without claiming credential ownership. Never emit credential values. Unrelated hosts and inactive accounts must not veto a working effective credential; do not gate admission on aggregate gh auth status.

- **R2 — Enforce explicit assignments on every runtime.** requireScmReady reads the assignment before cache or skip paths. Assigned host-gh requires the target-host store and rejects an applicable ambient token override even if it names the expected user. Assigned injected-token requires an applicable token and matching delivery correlation, without store fallback. Both require authenticated /user to match the recorded user login case-insensitively. A missing required assignment record or malformed assignment, source/delivery mismatches, and wrong users fail with specific remediation. Remove hostRuntimeAdmitsHostGh as an auth gate and recut #3663's runtime-denial tests; retain registry-before-skip/cache, source, delivery, and expected-login checks. Installation credentials cannot satisfy the current user-only assignment principal.

- **R3 — Admit usable installation authentication without claiming App identity.** A successful /user response with a valid login establishes user identity; compare it when one is explicitly required. With no required user, a successful well-formed GET /installation/repositories response may establish installation authentication, followed by a target repository check. A /user 403, token prefix, declared App name, gh auth status, or public repository GET alone is insufficient. Alternative probing succeeds only on positive authenticated evidence; failures otherwise remain failures. Installation success records no verified user login or issuing-App identity. It cannot satisfy a required user. Keep API host/version explicit and establish that the chosen installation probe rejects unauthenticated requests on supported hosts before relying on it. Network errors, revoked credentials, malformed responses, and missing repository access fail closed. Read readiness never claims permission to write; GitHub enforces permission on the actual operation. Selected-credential API results govern admission. Bare gh auth status, or a hostname-only check that still includes inactive accounts, must not reject an otherwise valid effective credential.

- **R4 — Bound the enforcement claim to named paths.** Apply the contract in packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.ts, packages/core/src/scm/readiness.ts, and the three existing deep callers: scm/main.ts, intake/issue-ingest-cli.ts, and intake/reconcile-issues-cli.ts. Add the same assignment/auth check immediately before pr-wait-mergeable/wrappers.ts::runGhMerge invokes its merge subprocess, using the operation's target and environment and retaining existing merge-policy gates. Mutation preflight must be fresh; an earlier ready-cache entry cannot authorize changed credentials, source, principal, or target. Failed preflight invokes no mutation subprocess. Direct gh/ghx, remote envelopes (#4997), release/gh.ts writers, and other subprocess paths are outside this issue's enforcement coverage; do not claim universal interception or blanket write authority.

- **R5 — Update the published policy together.** Update content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md §8, content/scm/github.md, content/contracts/scm-readiness.md, and content/patterns/multi-agent.md to state provisioning trust plus explicit assignment enforcement. Preserve the prohibition on substituting a maintainer account for an assigned worker. Replace blanket cloud host-store prohibitions, socket-absence grants, and the unconditional installation-token ban on covered paths. Propagate any changed pinned rule through content/templates/agents-entry.md and task agents:refresh. Include a brief CHANGELOG entry and explicit #3693/#3663 decision cross-references. Add no App-principal assignment type, token minter, or provenance attestation. Document the existing GROK_BUILD classifier disagreement as a diagnostic limitation; classifier unification is separate and cannot affect credential admission.

- **R6 — Cover the policy matrix and failures.** Test identical auth outcomes for local/CI/cloud/socket variants with identical target, assignment, and credentials; host-specific precedence including GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN; invalid-token no-fallback; unrelated-host token handling; stored/injected user success; unassigned installation success without claimed App identity; installation rejection for required users; missing/mismatched assignment/source/delivery/login; anonymous, malformed, and failed API probes; denied repository access; and operation denial after successful read readiness. Exercise all four named entry paths, changed-credential/target cache cases, registry-before-skip/cache ordering, and retained runtime diagnostics. Prove no mutation subprocess on preflight failure. Fixtures do not establish live cloud or installation-token success. Include valid-active/stale-inactive-account and valid-target/stale-other-host fixtures.

## Summary

The presumption is refuted for the **ambiguous Cursor marker**. It is not refuted for the **CI marker** or the **managed-probe** branch. The design's safety case says the principal compare now carries #983 for unregistered sessions. At the dispatch SHA that compare does not run on the unregistered path. So Design 1 (token presence only, for every runtime) removes a control that has no replacement. A narrower recut fixes the P1 rows without that loss.

## Anchor re-verification

All triage anchors reproduce by `git show` at the dispatch SHA:

- `packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.ts:103-108`: `inferGithubAuthMode` maps `cloud-headless` to `injected-token`, else `host-gh`. It does not read token env vars.
- `packages/core/src/intake/platform-capabilities.ts` `classifyRuntimeMode`: `CURSOR_AGENT` / `CURSOR_COMPOSER` without a managed read and without the opt-in returns `cloud-headless`, reason `cursor-marker-runtime-ambiguous`.
- `packages/core/src/platform/cursor-managed-runtime.ts:255-258`, `:60`, `:262`: as stated.
- `packages/core/src/scm/readiness.ts:256` and `:282-311`: as stated.
- `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:461`, `:465`, `:473` and `content/scm/github.md:406-427`: as stated.

The inventory is missing other runtime-label consumers (see F2, F3, F5).

## Findings

### F1 — blocks-the-design: the unregistered deep path has no principal compare

Evidence:

- All three deep callers pass `expectedPrincipal: null` explicitly: `packages/core/src/scm/main.ts:42-48`, `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest-cli.ts:44-48`, `packages/core/src/intake/reconcile-issues-cli.ts:43-47`.
- `resolveExpectedGithubWorkerPrincipal` (`github-auth-modes.ts` ~:228-243) returns `null` when `explicit === null`, **before** it reads `DEFT_EXPECTED_GITHUB_LOGIN`. So an operator cannot opt in to the compare on these verbs.
- The login compare (~:560) runs only when the expected principal is non-null. For the unregistered path, #3858 is the class ban only (installation `/user` 403 refused). It is not an identity check.

The issue's "Why the label is now redundant" table, row 2, says #3858 "runs [the #3665 expected-login compare] deep" on the three verbs. That is false at this SHA. "What this design gives up" says the preamble's purpose "is now enforced ... [by] the principal compare on the enforcing path". The unregistered path has no such seam.

Failure mode: a CI runner (`GITHUB_ACTIONS` / `BUILDKITE` / `CI`) or a Cursor-managed VM whose `hosts.yml` holds a **user-bearing** credential: a self-hosted runner, a baked image, or an earlier `gh auth login` by a maintainer. ## G1 — blocks-the-design: R0's `not-managed` grant hands host-gh to a managed VM on any 200 the probe does not recognise, and the probe requests a path the vendor does not document

**Evidence.**

- `bodyReportsManagedRuntime` (`cursor-managed-runtime.ts:119-139`) returns false for any body lacking a recognised `managed` field, and `readManagedRuntime` maps every 200 with such a body to `not-managed` (`:243-247`). Measured: `{"runtime":"machine"}` and the literal body `not json` both return `not-managed`. The module's own comment (`:114-117`) says the response shape "is documented only as agent/runtime is always managed" and that "over-matching here denies host credentials, which is the safe direction." R0 makes `not-managed` a grant, so that direction is now the unsafe one.
- The probe requests `/agent/runtime` (`:43`, `:211`). The vendor's every example uses the `/v1/meta-data/` prefix, and the installed Cursor 3.21.18 desktop bundle ships the constant `CURSOR_AGENT_METADATA_PATH_PREFIX = "/v1/meta-data"` beside `CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET_ENV_VAR` in the same `cloud-agent-identity` module. Nothing in the pinned tree knows that prefix. No positive read has ever been recorded (5389068843; #3859 tests stub the route).
- So on a real managed VM the verdict is whatever the metadata server returns for a path it does not document. A 404 is `unavailable` and R1 keeps that not-ready. A 200 with an index, an error object, or any other body is `not-managed`, and R0 grants host-gh.
- The vendor documents no environment that produces a 200 non-`managed` body: managed VMs always say `managed`, self-hosted workers serve nothing. Dropping the `not-managed` grant therefore costs no documented case.
- Marker decomposition: `recut3-no-socket` points at `:193-195`, which is the socket-unset branch only. The `not-managed` branch at `:243-247` is a second load-bearing premise under the same token, which the contract's decomposition rule refuses.

**Failure mode.** A Cursor-managed VM with the file-backed `ghs_` login, no token, socket at `/run/cursor/api.sock`. Deft probes `/agent/runtime`; the server answers 200 with a body that is not a recognised `managed` field (an index of keys, a JSON error, HTML). R0 classifies `cursor-marker-no-managed-socket`, selects `host-gh`, shallow `gh auth status` passes, session-start prints ready with an empty skip list, and the agent runs `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` under the App installation login. R4 ("row 2 stays closed") is false on that VM. No adversary and no same-user action is needed; the trust boundary sits on a third party's unknown-path behaviour. This is the A1 shape from 5819472093 re-entering through the branch the recut kept. P1 is not affected: desktop has the socket unset, so the fix below leaves the desktop grant intact.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind `recut3-no-socket` as written. Change the harvested Bound remedy: (a) R0 grants only when the socket env is unset or blank (the premise the marker already points at); (b) probe `not-managed` joins `unavailable` as not-ready under R1, with its own detail; (c) `MANAGED_RUNTIME_PATH` is corrected to the documented `/v1/meta-data/agent/runtime` in the same PR with a route fixture, so the R2 positive deny can fire, and the behaviour table states that no positive read has been measured on a real VM. What would flip this finding: a recorded positive `managed` read from a real managed VM at the path Deft requests, plus a documented statement that unknown paths do not return 200. Without both, `not-managed` cannot be a grant.

**Evidence.** R1: remediation "names what resolves it (`GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or a successful managed/not-managed read)". **Failure mode.** An operator on a socket-set not-ready session reads a remediation that says a managed read fixes it, gets a managed read, and stays not-ready with no further instruction. A builder following R1 literally either extends the report type silently or hardcodes the socket path into the remediation string.

**Disposition consequence.** R1 text: resolution is a token, or an env with the socket unset; a `managed` read is a deny, not a resolution. Name the report field that carries the probe detail (optional `runtimeModeDetail` on the intake report, or state that the remediation prints `MANAGED_RUNTIME_SOCKET_ENV` and the path from `env`). metadata.issueBody:
Policy recut, 2026-09-24. Review tree: 7234a9dd9231cc64a094a16f44c03080a713427e (fetched origin/HEAD). Replaces the socket-absence proposal in [recut 9](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/5016#issuecomment-5821317960). Previous comments remain the audit trail. This is a proposal, with no implementation or synthesis acceptance asserted.

## In plain English

Deft should use the GitHub credentials available in the environment the operator or platform has provided, including on a cloud machine. When a worker has an explicit credential-source and user assignment, it must honor that assignment. Cloud location alone is not a reason to reject working credentials.

This deliberately trusts provisioning. It does not prove who placed a credential on disk, identify which App minted an installation token, or detect an unintended account when no expected account was specified. GitHub still decides whether the credential may perform each requested operation.

## Pain (P1)

A local Cursor session with a working stored gh login can lose Deft's SCM-dependent gates because a runtime guess requires an injected token ([original report](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3656#issuecomment-5780268307)). Socket-absence exceptions narrow the symptom while continuing to reject otherwise usable cloud credentials.

The desired result is usable credentials on either machine type, with explicit assignments enforced. This is proposed behavior, not a measurement that current cloud sessions pass.

## Policy decision and scope

The operator approved provisioning trust in the current discussion and requested this recut and critique. Two prior decisions change together:

- #3693's blanket installation-token rejection is removed when no particular user identity is required. The issuing App remains unverified; an installation credential cannot satisfy a required user login.
- #3663's runtime veto on explicitly assigned host-gh workers is removed. Its registry, required source, delivery correlation, expected-user comparison, and refusal to substitute credentials remain.

This issue owns those bounded changes. Leaving either unchanged defeats the agreed cloud behavior. #983's worker-account separation still applies when an assignment requires it. Unassigned sessions accept effective environment credentials; they do not gain a fictitious intended-user comparison.

## Proposed remedy

- **R0 — Trust provisioning; do not authorize by runtime.** Unassigned processes use gh's effective credentials for the target host. Local, CI, cloud, ambiguous runtime, socket presence/absence, and probe failure have identical authentication policy. Remove DEFT_GITHUB_AUTH_MODE, hasExplicitHostGhSelection, EXPLICIT_SELECTION_REMEDIATION, and runtime/socket decisions from auth admission. Retain runtime diagnostics and unrelated runtime consumers. Do not add a replacement trust flag, socket exception, or platform allowlist.

- **R1 — Resolve the actual target and source.** Resolve the command's GitHub host and owner/repository with explicit target precedence over inferred context, consistently honoring gh's GH_REPO/GH_HOST and repository context. Probes and operations use the same resolved target and environment. For github.com and ghe.com subdomains, nonempty GH_TOKEN then GITHUB_TOKEN override the host's store; for GitHub Enterprise Server, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN then GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN do so. A token for another host family is neither this operation's injected source nor its source conflict. An applicable invalid token fails without fallback to stored credentials. Report the effective source without claiming credential ownership. Never emit credential values. Unrelated hosts and inactive accounts must not veto a working effective credential; do not gate admission on aggregate gh auth status.

- **R2 — Enforce explicit assignments on every runtime.** requireScmReady reads the assignment before cache or skip paths. Assigned host-gh requires the target-host store and rejects an applicable ambient token override even if it names the expected user. Assigned injected-token requires an applicable token and matching delivery correlation, without store fallback. Both require authenticated /user to match the recorded user login case-insensitively. A missing required assignment record or malformed assignment, source/delivery mismatches, and wrong users fail with specific remediation. Remove hostRuntimeAdmitsHostGh as an auth gate and recut #3663's runtime-denial tests; retain registry-before-skip/cache, source, delivery, and expected-login checks. Installation credentials cannot satisfy the current user-only assignment principal.

- **R3 — Admit usable installation authentication without claiming App identity.** A successful /user response with a valid login establishes user identity; compare it when one is explicitly required. With no required user, a successful well-formed GET /installation/repositories response may establish installation authentication, followed by a target repository check. A /user 403, token prefix, declared App name, gh auth status, or public repository GET alone is insufficient. Alternative probing succeeds only on positive authenticated evidence; failures otherwise remain failures. Installation success records no verified user login or issuing-App identity. It cannot satisfy a required user. Keep API host/version explicit and establish that the chosen installation probe rejects unauthenticated requests on supported hosts before relying on it. Network errors, revoked credentials, malformed responses, and missing repository access fail closed. Read readiness never claims permission to write; GitHub enforces permission on the actual operation. Selected-credential API results govern admission. Bare gh auth status, or a hostname-only check that still includes inactive accounts, must not reject an otherwise valid effective credential.

- **R4 — Bound the enforcement claim to named paths.** Apply the contract in packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.ts, packages/core/src/scm/readiness.ts, and the three existing deep callers: scm/main.ts, intake/issue-ingest-cli.ts, and intake/reconcile-issues-cli.ts. Add the same assignment/auth check immediately before pr-wait-mergeable/wrappers.ts::runGhMerge invokes its merge subprocess, using the operation's target and environment and retaining existing merge-policy gates. Mutation preflight must be fresh; an earlier ready-cache entry cannot authorize changed credentials, source, principal, or target. Failed preflight invokes no mutation subprocess. Direct gh/ghx, remote envelopes (#4997), release/gh.ts writers, and other subprocess paths are outside this issue's enforcement coverage; do not claim universal interception or blanket write authority.

- **R5 — Update the published policy together.** Update content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md §8, content/scm/github.md, content/contracts/scm-readiness.md, and content/patterns/multi-agent.md to state provisioning trust plus explicit assignment enforcement. Preserve the prohibition on substituting a maintainer account for an assigned worker. Replace blanket cloud host-store prohibitions, socket-absence grants, and the unconditional installation-token ban on covered paths. Propagate any changed pinned rule through content/templates/agents-entry.md and task agents:refresh. Include a brief CHANGELOG entry and explicit #3693/#3663 decision cross-references. Add no App-principal assignment type, token minter, or provenance attestation. Document the existing GROK_BUILD classifier disagreement as a diagnostic limitation; classifier unification is separate and cannot affect credential admission.

- **R6 — Cover the policy matrix and failures.** Test identical auth outcomes for local/CI/cloud/socket variants with identical target, assignment, and credentials; host-specific precedence including GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN; invalid-token no-fallback; unrelated-host token handling; stored/injected user success; unassigned installation success without claimed App identity; installation rejection for required users; missing/mismatched assignment/source/delivery/login; anonymous, malformed, and failed API probes; denied repository access; and operation denial after successful read readiness. Exercise all four named entry paths, changed-credential/target cache cases, registry-before-skip/cache ordering, and retained runtime diagnostics. Prove no mutation subprocess on preflight failure. Fixtures do not establish live cloud or installation-token success. Include valid-active/stale-inactive-account and valid-target/stale-other-host fixtures.

## Behavior after implementation

| Situation | Result on covered paths |
| --- | --- |
| Unassigned desktop or cloud, valid stored user login | Uses that login without runtime/socket opt-in |
| Unassigned desktop or cloud, valid installation credential | Proceeds after installation-authentication and target checks; App identity unknown |
| Assigned host-gh worker on cloud, expected stored user, no applicable override | Proceeds after user match |
| Assigned user worker with installation credential | Refuses: required user not satisfied |
| Assigned source missing, overridden, or wrong user | Refuses without substitution |
| Applicable injected token invalid, stored login valid | Refuses; no fallback |
| No usable credentials or target access | Refuses with source/host-specific remediation |
| Read readiness passes but write permission is absent | GitHub rejects the operation |

## Evidence and corrections

At the pinned tree, inferGithubAuthMode selects from runtime, enforceRegisteredWorker independently denies cloud host-gh, and validateAfterAuth unconditionally rejects recognized installation /user failures. These are separate decisions. The three deep callers pass expectedPrincipal: null for unregistered sessions; the registry supplies the expected user for assigned workers. runGhMerge has no matching auth guard today. These are code readings, not live cloud measurements.

Earlier claims that every unregistered session already compared an intended principal and that writes stayed blocked everywhere were incorrect. Earlier socket-route/default-path findings were valid objections to the old heuristic; this policy removes the heuristic from authorization rather than proving its vendor assumptions. The previous R0-R6 extraction loss was a recording defect: successor remedies must be complete and independently harvestable.

Primary references: [gh host and environment precedence](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment), [installation repositories endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/apps/installations#list-repositories-accessible-to-the-app-installation). The endpoint documentation includes a public-resource caveat. An unauthenticated github.com request with API version 2022-11-28 returned 401 in this review on 2026-09-24. That single negative control does not establish all host/version behavior. No live installation-token success has been measured in this recut.

## Exclusions and tradeoff

Credential provenance, hostile same-user credential/config replacement, comprehensive direct-command interception (#4997), token-output hardening (#3664), App-identity attestation, and runtime-probe repair remain separate work. No issue is closed by this recut. An unassigned process can use an unintended yet valid account if its environment was prepared incorrectly. Operators requiring a particular worker account must supply an explicit assignment; a cloud label supplies neither an assignment nor proof of trust.
